=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:lines 157 and 1927-1933 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: CHECK_RUNS_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECS is set to 120 in the workflow while README.md documents 1200, so the collector times out far sooner than documented and can miss completed failures/log tails.
  WHY: The documented 20-minute wait becomes only 2 minutes, which reduces the chance that failed check-runs reach completion before the snapshot is taken.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:lines 158 and 1931-1935 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: CHECK_RUNS_POLL_INTERVAL_SECS is set to 30 in the workflow while README.md documents 20, so the collector polls less frequently than documented.
  WHY: Fewer polls before timeout means fewer opportunities for check-runs to complete; the reviewer noted this is a materially different polling cadence.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:`fetch_log_tail()` (lines ~2066-2092) — subprocess call to `gh run view` per failed check-run | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: Fetching a log tail for every failed check-run can push the reviewer/editor embed budget over the limit and truncate the log_tail content without warning.
  WHY: With several failures, the accumulated tail data can exceed the roughly 80K context budget and cut off the most important failure lines.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:Python `fetch_log_tail` function (lines ~2065-2095 in current snapshot, added in PR) + the `subprocess.run(..., timeout=60)` | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: A timed-out `gh run view` call is caught and discarded without explicitly cleaning up the spawned process.
  WHY: Repeated timeouts can leave zombie/orphan processes behind and eventually exhaust process or memory resources in the workflow job.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:lines 2049-2053 (Python env var parsing) + the call site at line ~2089 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `CHECK_RUNS_LOG_TAIL_BYTES` is read from `os.environ` in a way that can silently diverge from later workflow/job overrides.
  WHY: A future override could use a stale/default byte limit, changing whether log tails are emitted and how large they are without the writer noticing.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:`fetch_log_tail` + the loop `for i, r in enumerate(failed):` (around line 2115) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The code unconditionally issues one `gh run view --log --job <id>` call per failed check-run, which can blow up API usage and prompt size under multiple failures.
  WHY: Several simultaneous failures can consume the reviewer/editor context budget and increase latency enough to make autofix runs less effective.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh (lines 663-669 and 803-816) + scripts/review_run_reviewers.sh (lines 439-445, 491-497) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The prompt embedding logic was not adjusted for potentially large `log_tail` sections, so the embedded check-run context can still be truncated mid-tail.
  WHY: Malformed or partial log-tail context can prevent the model from mapping failures correctly and can lead to no-op or incorrect fixes.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
